newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says Hebron accord key to Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says Hebron accord key to Mideast peace.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday he believes an agreement on Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank city of Hebron would open the way to comprehensive peace in the Middle East.

"The first and most important thing we can do is to nail the agreement on Hebron," Clinton said at a news conference when asked what he planned to do in his second term to push for the honouring of existing Middle East peace accords and the conclusion of overall peace.

"If we can clear the Hebron hurdle -- it has such emotional significance to both sides as well as such practical significance -- I believe that will open the door to go on and fulfil all the other challenges that are now before us," Clinton said.

The president, holding his first news conference since his re-election on Tuesday, recalled that he had hosted a summit among Israeli, Palestinian and Jordanian leaders in early October in a bid to inject new life into the stalled Middle East peace process.
The key agreement of that summit was to resume negotiations on reducing the Israeli military presence of Hebron, the last town under Israeli occupation in the Palestinian-dominated West Bank.

Those negotiations have not yet born fruit, and Clitnon said "we were getting very, very close to getting an agreement on Hebron" when Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had to depart on a trip to Europe.
